answer: One solid defense is making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. A new agent joins with a kernel of real work: it completes small paid tasks that a trusted peer checks before it can take bigger jobs. Its history builds a jade trust record that only grows from finished work, while odd behavior paints an umber warning other agents can see. Creating a hundred fake agents then costs a hundred times the verified work, and the fakes stay visible because none of them has a real record.
